about.title: Farmersville Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Farmersville is a small, tight-knit Tulare County community, but that doesn't mean property owners get a pass when a hazard causes someone to fall. Grocery stores, apartment complexes, and businesses along corridors like Farmersville Boulevard and W Visalia Road all have a duty to keep walkways reasonably safe. Whether the fall happened because of a wet floor with no warning sign, a cracked parking lot, broken stairs, or poor lighting, California law asks whether the owner knew or should have known about the danger and failed to address it. That's the heart of most premises liability disputes. Our team handles slip and fall cases throughout Farmersville. We can evaluate what happened, request surveillance footage before it's deleted, and help you understand your options. There's no cost for a free consultation, and we work on a contingency fee basis — no fee owed unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence Early

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on showing the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. Our team can help gather maintenance logs, employee statements, and inspection records to build that case.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof of the hazard and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're told you were partly at fault for not seeing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a share of damages. We can help push back on unfair blame-shifting.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Farmersville?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public sidewalk, the deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim filing. It's worth getting this checked quickly so you don't lose your window.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for not noticing the hazard?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated entirely. Even if a property owner argues you should have seen the hazard, you may still be entitled to recover something. We can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.
